elements.quote: Worldwide, surgery related deaths within 30 days of the procedure accounts the third contributor among all causes of deaths, with an estimated 4.2 million people annually and half of these deaths occur in low and middle income countries.
elements.reason: Provides a brief statement of the global burden of surgery-related deaths, offering some context about the problem, but does not describe the current state of knowledge specifically about surgical site infection after cesarean section or articulate important uncertainties.

elements.quote: Wehave checked the PROSPERO database https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/displayrecord.php?) to see whether recently published or ongoing projects exist related to the topic to avoid any further unnecessary duplication: This systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in the PROSPERO database with ID no. CRD42023442583. A SRMA was conducted on SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: States that the review was registered and that the review concerns SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia, implying a decision to conduct the review and avoidance of duplication; however it does not explicitly explain the clinical/public health importance or the specific need for this review in detail.

elements.quote: Wehave checked the PROSPERO database https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/displayrecord.php?) to see whether recently published or ongoing projects exist related to the topic to avoid any further unnecessary duplication: This systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in the PROSPERO database with ID no. CRD42023442583.
elements.reason: Although the authors report checking PROSPERO to avoid duplication and registered the review, there is no explicit statement describing the need for this review in the context of any existing similar systematic reviews, nor are previous reviews cited or discussed.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: The review focuses on prevalence and predictors from observational studies rather than intervention effects, so describing mechanisms of intervention action is not applicable.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: The review does not evaluate complex interventions or delivery contexts; it synthesizes observational prevalence and association data, so a logic model for intervention components is not applicable.

elements.quote: To determine the pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The review states an explicit objective describing the aim (pooled prevalence and predictors of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia). However, there is no evidence that the objective is framed using a recognized question-formulation framework (e.g., PICO), so the requirement for using a relevant framework is only partially met.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: The conditional item applies to reviews of intervention effects. The manuscript is a prevalence/observational factors SRMA (not an intervention effects review), so specifying planned comparisons using PICO is not applicable.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies setting (regional states of Ethiopia) and eligible study designs (observational: case-control, cross-sectional, cohort noted elsewhere), and outcome (SSI). It does not report follow-up requirements or other question-framework components (e.g., participant characteristics or duration of follow-up), so the description is incomplete.

elements.quote: Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies report characteristics: publication status (published and grey literature), language (English), and a time window (Jan 1, 2013 to Sep 2023).

The authors state that articles which 'lack our outcome of interest' were excluded, but do not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Based on the study region, subgroup analyses were done.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies groups used in syntheses (subgroup analyses by study region) and uses these in the analyses, linking groupings (regions) to the syntheses.
The manuscript imposes restrictions (e.g., English language, date range) but does not provide rationales for these notable eligibility restrictions.

elements.quote: The electronic literature search was last performed on September 23, 2023.
elements.reason: A specific last-search date for the electronic literature search is reported, but the manuscript does not report the date when each individual information source (each database, register, website, etc.) was last searched; only an overall search date is given.

elements.quote: An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done.
elements.reason: The names of multiple bibliographic databases are listed, but the manuscript does not report the search interface/platform used for each database nor the coverage dates for each database.

elements.quote: 'An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013. ... Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and key terms had been developed using different Boolean operators 'AND' and 'OR'. The following search terms were used: '(prevalence) OR (magnitude) OR (proportion) OR (epidemiology) OR (surgical site infection) OR (surgical site) OR (wound infection) AND (cesarean section) OR (cesarean delivery) OR (post cesarean section) AND (determinants) OR (associated factors) OR (risk factors) OR (predictors) AND (Ethiopia)'. The electronic literature search was last performed on September 23, 2023.'
elements.reason: The manuscript lists databases searched, a combined search string, and the date of the last search, but does not provide the complete, database-specific search strategies as actually run for each database (no separate search strings or syntax for individual sources).

elements.quote: 'Both published and unpublished literatures conducted on the prevalence and/or the factors associated with the development of SSI following cesarean delivery in Ethiopia were searched via two authors (ES and MA). Eligible literatures in English language only were identified. An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013.'
elements.reason: The manuscript reports search limits (English language, searched since 2013) but does not describe or justify these limits by reference to the eligibility criteria (no rationale given).
No citation or description of published search approaches or filters and no description of any adaptations are provided in the retrieved evidence.
No mention of natural-language processing or text-analysis tools used to identify or refine search terms is present in the provided evidence.
No tools used to translate search strings between sources are specified in the available text.
There is no description of any validation of the search strategy or validation studies in the retrieved evidence.
No information about peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) or the process/tool used is provided in the supplied evidence.

elements.quote: 'Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and key terms had been developed using different Boolean operators 'AND' and 'OR'. The following search terms were used: ...'
elements.reason: The manuscript does not state that the search structure was not based on PICO nor describe a final conceptual structure or explorations used to develop it; no such description is provided.

elements.quote: Atotal of 6334 articles were found by using our search strategies: Google scholar, pub-med, Hinari, EMBASE, Scopus and Medline. After 1398 articles were removed for the reason of duplication, 4932 articles left. Then by reviewing their titles and abstracts, 4800 and 100 articles were removed respectively. Finally 32 full text papers were accessed and evaluated for the predefined inclusion criteria. Thus 13 more articles were excluded for the afore-mentioned reasons. Eventually, 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA (Fig 1).
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the number of records at each screening stage (duplicates removed, titles/abstracts excluded, full texts assessed, final included), but it does not state the number of reviewers who screened records and full reports.
No explicit statement that reviewers worked independently at each screening stage (screening of records or full-texts) is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data using standardized data extraction format developed according to 2014 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Reviewers' manual [24]. Any disagreement between reviewers was resolved by the third author (AA). Consensus was declared through critical discussion and evaluation of the articles by all the independent reviewers.
elements.reason: The process for resolving disagreements is described: a third author resolved disagreements and consensus was reached through discussion and evaluation.

elements.quote: This SRMA has comprised of two main outcomes. The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum and it could be at least one of the following: ( A superficial incisional , deep incisional or deep/organ SSI) . The secondary outcome was the determinants of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists and defines the outcome domains (primary: magnitude of SSI with CDC definition and types; secondary: determinants of SSI).

elements.quote: The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum
elements.reason: The time frame for the primary outcome is specified as within 30 days postpartum.

elements.reason: Outcomes are prioritized (primary and secondary) and defined, but no rationale is provided for why the primary outcome was considered most important for interpretation.

elements.quote: we used Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment scale (NOS) adapted for observational studies to assess the quality of each study included in this SRMA [25] (S1 Table).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly names the risk-of-bias/quality assessment tool (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, adapted for observational studies).

elements.reason: The domains/components assessed by the NOS (Selection, Comparability, Outcome) and their point allocations are specified.

elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias/quality judgement is reported (scores and interpretation: 8–9 indicate good quality), indicating rules used to derive overall judgments.

In the case of disagreement between two authors; another third author (AA, WS and BB) were involved and discussed and resolved the disagreement.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two), their independence (they assessed each study; disagreements resolved by a third author), and the disagreement-resolution procedure are reported.
No information is provided about contacting study investigators or procedures to obtain/confirm risk-of-bias information from authors.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment (use, training, performance, validation) are described.

elements.quote: A random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI. Adjusted Odds Ratio (OR) with 95% Confidence Interval (CI) was also considered to determine the association of identified variables with SSI.
elements.reason: The methods explicitly state the effect measures used for the primary synthesis (pooled prevalence via random-effects model) and for associations (adjusted odds ratios with 95% CIs).
No thresholds or ranges used to interpret effect size (e.g., categorizations of effect magnitude) or rationale for such thresholds are reported in the provided evidence.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure (e.g., converting ORs to risk ratios) are described in the retrieved evidence.
No justification for the choice of effect measures (why pooled prevalence and adjusted OR were chosen) is provided in the available text.

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA. Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023. Exclusion. which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA. On the other hand, literatures with poor quality as per the criteria of reviewing articles were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies inclusion and exclusion criteria (study population, outcomes of interest, study designs, publication types, language, date range, and exclusion of poor-quality studies), which describes the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for the review and thus for inclusion in the syntheses.

elements.quote: All the datasets were exported to Mendeley reference manager, and then we transferred to the Microsoft Excel spreadsheet to remove duplicate data in the review. Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data using standardized data extraction format developed according to 2014 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Reviewers' manual [24]. Any disagreement between reviewers was resolved by the third author (AA). Consensus was declared through critical discussion and evaluation of the articles by all the independent reviewers. The name of the author, sample size, publication year, study region, study design, prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection, and adjusted odds ratio with its 95% CI of the factors associated with SSI.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data management steps (exporting to Mendeley, transfer to Excel, duplicate removal) and the variables extracted (including adjusted ORs and 95% CIs) using a standardized form, which are methods to prepare data for synthesis. However, it does not describe specific methods for handling missing summary statistics or any data conversions/imputations (e.g., procedures for missing CIs, transformations), so the reporting is incomplete.

elements.quote: The name of the author, sample size, publication year, study region, study design, prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection, and adjusted odds ratio with its 95% CI of the factors associated with SSI.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the data items extracted and therefore the data included in tabular displays (author, sample size, year, region, design, prevalence, AOR with 95% CI), fulfilling the requirement to describe tabular structures and included data.

elements.quote: Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias. ... A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI. To identify determinant factors, we used the pooled AOR in forest plot format with its respective 95%CI.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the graphical methods used (funnel plot, Egger's test, forest plots for pooled prevalence and pooled AORs), describing how results were visually displayed.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was done based on the study region. A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the basis for grouping studies (subgroup analysis by study region) and presents grouped results in forest plots, thus reporting the ordering/grouping used in tables/graphs.
No non-standard graphical methods are reported (only standard forest plots and funnel plots are described), so a rationale for non-standard graphs is not applicable.

elements.quote: Statistical analysis was conducted using STATA version 17 software.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly reports the software and version used for statistical synthesis (STATA version 17).
A meta-analysis was performed in this review (pooled prevalence and pooled AOR); therefore methods for alternative synthesis when meta-analysis was not possible do not apply.

elements.quote: Therefore we have used the random effect model to resolve the issue of heterogeneity between included studies.
elements.reason: The manuscript states the meta-analysis model used (random-effects) and gives a rationale (to address/resolve substantial heterogeneity).

elements.quote: Then random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia. ... A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI. To identify determinant factors, we used the pooled AOR in forest plot format with its respective 95%CI.
elements.reason: The statistical synthesis approach is described: random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence and pooled adjusted odds ratios, with results presented as forest plots and 95% CIs.

elements.quote: Cochrane Q-test and I 2 statistics were computed to assess heterogeneity among all the studies included in this SRMA. ... Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias.
elements.reason: Methods to identify and quantify heterogeneity are reported (Cochrane Q-test and I2); publication bias methods (funnel plot, Egger's) are also described.
No information is provided about which between-study variance estimator (e.g. DerSimonian–Laird, REML) was used for the random-effects meta-analysis.
The manuscript does not report the specific method used to calculate confidence intervals for the summary effect in the random-effects meta-analysis.
No additional implementation details for the random-effects model (e.g. weighting scheme, small-sample corrections) are reported.
The review did not perform a Bayesian meta-analysis, so reporting of prior distributions is not applicable.
There is no description of methods to account for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study (e.g., multilevel models, robust variance estimation).
The manuscript does not identify any planned syntheses that were judged impossible or inappropriate nor provides reasons for such judgments.

elements.quote: Based on the study region, subgroup analyses were done. The stability or robustness of the pooled estimates to outliers and the impact of individual studies were assessed using sensitivity analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states methods used to explore heterogeneity: subgroup analyses by study region and sensitivity analysis to assess influence of individual studies/outliers.

elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was done by using the study region and the result revealed that the pooled prevalence of SSI cesarean section was highest in Amhara region (12.47%; 95% (CI: 7.33, 17.60%), I 2 = 95.28%, P = 0.00) followed by SNNP region (11.76%; 95% (CI: 10.29, 13.22%), I 2 = 0.00%, P = 0.86). on the contrary, the lowest prevalence of SSI after cesarean section was observed in Tigray region (8.91%; 95%CI: 4.15, 13.66%), I 2 = 72.24%, P = 0.06) followed by Oromia region (9.18%; 95%CI: 7.16, 11.20%), I 2 = 0.00%, P = 0.77 (Fig 4).
elements.reason: Factors and factor levels are reported (study region with region-specific pooled estimates), but the manuscript does not state any expected direction of effect modification.
No statement specifies whether subgroup/meta-regression analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both.
The manuscript reports statistical tests comparing subgroup effects (Cochran's Q test with Q-statistics and p-values) for subgroup comparisons.
No description is provided of informal methods to explore heterogeneity used when meta-analysis was unsuitable (no factors/levels or narrative approaches described).
The manuscript does not identify whether any heterogeneity analyses were not pre-specified (no statement labeling analyses as post-hoc or exploratory).

elements.quote: The stability or robustness of the pooled estimates to outliers and the impact of individual studies were assessed using sensitivity analysis.
elements.reason: The manuscript states that sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess robustness to outliers and the impact of individual studies, and further reports that the pooled prevalence was not influenced by a single study (text_21). However, it does not provide detailed information about the exact sensitivity analyses performed (e.g., methods, specific analyses, criteria for outlier removal), so details of every sensitivity analysis are not fully reported.

There is no indication in the provided evidence that any sensitivity analyses were non–pre-specified or that non–pre-specified analyses were identified as such. The report does not state whether sensitivity analyses were pre-specified.

elements.quote: Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias. The p-value > 0.05 indicated that there was no publication bias.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the statistical methods (funnel plot and Egger's test) used to assess publication bias (risk of bias due to missing results).
No information is provided about using an existing reporting-bias assessment tool's specific domains/items or how an overall judgment was derived.
